interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: The prognosis is influenced by several documented factors. Favorable findings include a negative surgical margin and absence of seminal vesicle invasion, with no lymphovascular invasion noted. The pathological stage was pT2 without extraprostatic extension. Countervailing factors include the preoperative PSA of 11.4 and the absence of nodal sampling, which widens uncertainty regarding nodal status. The discrepancy between the single biopsy and the prostatectomy specimen, specifically the missing Gleason pattern and ISUP report, also contributes to uncertainty. The current horizon suggests a follow-up period of approximately 71 months without an event. Postoperative PSA and its trajectory are critical missing pieces of information that would significantly revise this assessment. Missing nodal sampling further complicates the certainty of the overall outcome. The fixed estimated horizon is 70.80 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 46.02–95.58 months; its coverage has not been validated.
